title: TTL mismatch in routing + control-plane backpressure caused regional load spike and SLO breach
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-14 we experienced a multi-region incident that caused a sustained SLO miss for 22 minutes for the inference API. Traffic skewed toward eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1; requests saw 95th and 99th percentile latency increases and progressive load shedding in secondary regions. Root cause was a routing table TTL mismatch combined with control-plane backpressure that amplified failover decisions and caused circuit breakers to open aggressively, starving healthy capacity and triggering cascading degradations.
timeline: 2026-02-14T17:22:00Z - First elevated 95p latency alert for eu-west-1; 17:24:00Z - automated failover to secondary regions begins; 17:25:30Z - control-plane started signalling stale route refreshes due to stale TTL values; 17:26:45Z - circuit breakers began hysteresis oscillation: several nodes opened then closed rapidly; 17:28:00Z - adaptive load shedding engaged in ap-southeast-1; 17:40:00Z - emergency mitigation applied (revert control-plane throttle + manual route flush); 17:44:00Z - traffic rebalanced and latency began returning toward baseline; 17:48:00Z - all circuits stable; incident declared resolved at 17:52:00Z. Total SLO breach window: 17:22:00Z - 17:44:00Z (22 minutes).
impact: Customer-facing latency and error-rate increase for text-generation endpoints in impacted regions, increased token cost due to retries, and automated load shedding that dropped best-effort requests. Several paying customers experienced degraded throughput and observed 5xx spikes on dashboards tied to hosted API. Internal PagerDuty was triggered; post-incident ticketing and customer outreach initiated.
root_cause: A TTL mismatch between the control-plane route cache and the data-plane routing table caused the data-plane to serve stale affinity maps. During a routine capacity fluctuation, the control-plane applied a conservative backpressure (rate-limiting route refresh RPCs) which prevented timely invalidation of stale routes. Stale routes caused disproportionate traffic to some shards; those shards hit local CPU/GPU queues and the circuit-breaker hysteresis logic opened aggressively. The opened circuits redirected more requests to remaining healthy shards, creating amplification and triggering automated load-shedding thresholds.
contributing_factors: routing table TTL config drift introduced during a previous rollout (runtime-1.20) was not captured in the config test-suite
control-plane throttling threshold was tuned to prefer stability over rapid route refresh, which delayed invalidation during load shifts
circuit-breaker hysteresis window not tuned for fast rotating routes (short TTLs), causing oscillation
insufficient observability around control-plane route-refresh latency and TTL mismatch (no dedicated alert)
runbook for combined control-plane + data-plane route mismatch was outdated and lacked playbook steps for manual route flush
immediate_mitigation: Manually flushed data-plane routing caches in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 (Miguel O., 17:40Z)
Temporarily disabled aggressive control-plane backpressure to allow route refreshes to proceed (Sana L., 17:41Z)
Raised circuit-breaker cool-down window to reduce oscillation while route caches warmed (Thomas N., 17:42Z)
Applied temporary per-region rate-limit for new best-effort requests to limit amplification (On-call infra, 17:43Z)
long_term_actions: ACTION-1: Add automated config validation to detect TTL/comment drift between control-plane and data-plane configs; owner: Infrastructure Config Team (Sana Li); due: 2026-03-15
ACTION-2: Add end-to-end synthetic that exercises route refresh and TTL expiry under load and alert when route-refresh latency > 3s; owner: SRE (Thomas Nguyen); due: 2026-03-10

ACTION-3: Revisit circuit-breaker hysteresis for short-lived route changes; implement adaptive hysteresis that considers recent route-flush events; owner: Serving Runtime (Miguel Ortega); estimate: 5 pts; due: 2026-03-22
ACTION-4: Instrument and surface a TTL-mismatch alert (control-plane vs data-plane) in Console with automated triage links and runbook; owner: Observability (Priya Kapoor); due: 2026-03-08
ACTION-5: Update runbook with explicit manual route-flush instructions and coordination steps between control-plane and data-plane owners; owner: Oncall Docs (Asha Patel); due: 2026-03-01

ACTION-6: Add a graceful partial-failover policy that limits amplification by spreading traffic and enforcing soft-queues before opening circuits; owner: Traffic Orchestration (Samir Desai); due: 2026-04-05
notes: Reviewed in postmortem review on 2026-02-20: PM and Design noted need to communicate SLA windows more clearly to customers (feedback from Customer Success)
Security reviewed: no customer data exfiltration; controls validated (security signoff by R. Martinez on 2026-02-22)
SRE approved long-term actions and timeline; follow-up review scheduled 2026-03-16
follow_up_actions: Schedule cross-team runbook war-room to rehearse manual route flush + control-plane throttle coordination (owner: Asha Patel; due: 2026-03-01)
Track ACTION-1 through CONFIG-PIPELINE board and ensure automated tests are merged before runtime-1.23 cutoff
Ensure customers affected by the incident receive a tailored incident summary and remediation steps (owner: Customer Reliability Engineering; due: 2026-02-28)

Sana L.: Observability gap was the main contributor; will prioritize TTL mismatch alerting and synthetic tests
